A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original certified-training experiments, Pareto-front comparisons, hyperparameter analyses, verification timings, and repeated-seed results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds an MTL-IBP parameter-sweep comparison alongside revised validation-set results.

M1.justification: The constrained Bayesian optimisation, incomplete-verification proxy, clustering, and final complete-verification procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 repairs variable and set expressions to match the existing description. The BatchNorm wording correction agrees with the architecture already specified in v1's Appendix E.3 and Table 5.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, Tiny ImageNet, and MNIST under the same classification tasks and perturbation radii. The new parameter sweep uses existing CIFAR-10 scenarios; it adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D.8 and new Figure 11 add an evaluated baseline that sweeps MTL-IBP's trade-off parameter α while fixing other hyperparameters to De Palma et al. (2024b)'s configurations. Existing certified-training comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The validation-set study changes from incomplete verification to complete verification with a 1,000-second per-instance timeout, retaining the 20% validation split. The new baseline evaluates 20 logarithmically spaced α values between 10^-6 and 1 using CROWN verification and fixed remaining hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The new α-sweep analysis tests whether varying the loss trade-off parameter alone can match joint hyperparameter optimisation, for MTL-IBP at two CIFAR-10 radii. The existing validation-versus-test tuning analysis is also revised using complete verification; other supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three optimisation seeds, the three-seed evaluation with means and standard-deviation bars in Figure 10, and the ±0.5 comparison criterion in Appendix D.7. No uncertainty-estimation or statistical-testing procedure is added or changed.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 8 replace the validation-study results under a different verification procedure, so their higher certified accuracies are not same-setting gains. At ε = 8/255, strict test-tuning dominance becomes 'almost always' dominance. New Figure 11 reports competitiveness with the α-sweep baseline and some better trade-offs at ε = 2/255. Existing benchmark tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects the complexity classification of the exact optimisation problem from NP-complete to NP-hard. Algorithm 1 repairs the constrained Pareto-set expressions. The underlying mathematical development and EHVI formulation are otherwise retained, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusions retain the same contributions: Pareto-front evaluation, joint hyperparameter optimisation, previously undertuned methods, limited progress at larger radii, and complementary strengths among certified-training methods.

C2.justification: The validation discussion drops the argument that similarly shaped fronts imply preserved relative performance, and Appendix D.3 qualifies universal dominance. Appendix D.8 adds interpretation concerning expert-tuning requirements, hyperparameter interactions, and the baseline's applicability only to methods with explicit trade-off parameters.

D1.justification: Appendix D.8 documents the new sweep's parameter range, sampling, fixed configurations, and verifier. Appendix E.4 corrects BatchNorm placement from after to before activations, resolving an existing inconsistency. Algorithm 1 clarifies evaluation of the selected candidate. Hardware, software versions, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B.2 expands the discussion of automated configuration in neural-network verification, adding Kaulen and Hoos (2026) and discussing the already-cited König et al. (2022). The broader positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording, grammar, bibliography, and pseudocode cross-reference corrections, adds Appendix D.8, and modestly expands related work. The narrative and overall section structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 8 receive revised plots, axes, and captions, and Figure 11 adds the baseline comparison. Existing appendix figures and tables are rearranged, with subsequent figures renumbered and the timeout plots resized. Most visual material is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a useful direct comparison against a simpler tuning alternative and aligns the validation study with the main complete-verification criterion. Technical and pseudocode corrections improve accuracy and reproducibility. These are limited improvements: the new baseline covers only MTL-IBP on CIFAR-10, and Section 5's blanket dominance wording is not fully reconciled with the exceptions acknowledged in Appendix D.3.
